overview.text: Python is a general-purpose programming language: people use it to give computers instructions, build programs, and automate tasks. Guido van Rossum began creating it in December 1989 as a language influenced by ABC; he chose “Python” as a working title while a fan of the comedy show Monty Python’s Flying Circus. A defining feature is that indentation—the spaces at the start of a line—groups related statements into code blocks. Van Rossum said this design helps make programs more readable. Python is interpreted and has an extensive standard library, along with third-party modules, giving programmers ready-made tools for many kinds of projects.

key_facts.text: Python’s creator, Guido van Rossum, started the project in December 1989 and named it after Monty Python’s Flying Circus, not the snake.
Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that supports several programming styles, including object-oriented, procedural, and functional programming.
Indentation determines how Python groups statements; inconsistent indentation can cause an error.
Python’s interpreter runs code, and the language’s extensive standard library supplies modules for common tasks; programmers can also use third-party modules.
Van Rossum said indentation reduces visual clutter and encourages a more uniform style, helping people read one another’s code.
